Oh, I dunno. Having played the MGX games, the MGS games, and even some of the boring mobile ones (Acid, I'm looking at you), this one was actually pretty fun and a bit more cohesive in terms of story. Generally, Kojima has trouble containing his lust for mecha porn but he held off until the very end which was pretty classy. I felt it made a nice buildup for the entire game.

As for the whole body double thing.. well.. I had my suspicions throughout the game. For some reason, I had the feeling that Venom Snake simply didn't look like Big Boss (facial reconstruction from the accident aside). The shape was a bit off and so was the nose. There were other hints along the way as well. I think the whole "punch to the gut" thing was the point though. As far as your complaint about the story feeling incomplete, they did have to rush towards the end because Konami tore apart Kojima Productions and had them finish the game as contractors, which is why after MGSV I'm never buying a Konami game again. They didn't let the man finish his magnum opus. That's also why there are some missing missions and cutscenes in MGSV. That aside, the story did tie up decently but you have to literally complete every single thing and remember all the tiny details. Unlike previous MGS games they didn't have time to tie everything up with a bow to that it was all covered perfectly and the audience was aware of it. However, all that aside, MGSV does hold up storyline wise.

MGSV tied up the overall story nicely since Big Boss was literally the greatest soldier to ever live and Venom Snake is a crucial part of that. Prior to MGSV when Big Boss was still part of the Patriots, Zero had spread a ton of stories about Big Boss. Some of them true, some slight fabrications, and others were complete lies. Big Boss had to lie low after the original Mother Base was destroyed, right? Well, in order to come back he basically needed to recreate a lot of the myth surrounding him so that the world would accept the fact that he didn't die. Obviously, coming back out as himself would be way too risky and so they turned the MSF medic from Ground Zeroes into the "real" Big Boss so that Venom Snake could work to recreate MSF in the form of Diamond Dogs and further the legend of Big Boss while the real Big Boss worked behind the scenes on other projects, specifically getting back in with the US. I say this because aside from the whole Frank Jaeger thing (read Gray Fox pre-MG1), Big Boss also returned to the US to take control of FOXHOUND and train Solid Snake, who was his clone-baby (which he was aware of). Not to mention that Snake ended up killing "Big Boss" in that game only for him to return in MG2. Solid defeating Venom was all part of the plan as it allowed the real Big Boss to return and take control of the remains of what was once Diamond Dogs.

So, when you take Big Boss at face value, this guy has been "killed" many times and continues to return and continues to sock it to his enemies and fight for what he believes in. Venom Snake helped a lot with that. The main reason that Venom Snake seemed like such a lifeless character, IMHO, was because he wasn't Big Boss. He was just some badass MSF medic that got thrust into the hands of fate. Unlike previous Big Boss era MGS games, there weren't a lot of references to The Boss or the ideals that Big Boss tried to uphold. It was literally all Miller and Ocelot pulling the strings and the funny thing is that Miller didn't even know for the longest time. Ocelot knew, which is why, like always, he played everyone like a fucking fiddle. That's just who Ocelot was.

So yeah, you didn't play as Big Boss and Venom Snake had know real character presence outside of a few memorable moments in cutscenes and cassette tapes. Well, as stated, that's because he was just some dude being used by someone else. That's essentially what the entire series is about anyway. MGSV was simply part of the tale that made Big Boss so special in the overall series and it served as the final tie between the Big Boss era games and the Metal Gear games that originally began the series.
